candidates.issues: Baking a wet batter with only 1 tbsp of oil will likely result in a gummy rather than truly crispy crust.
Milk in the wet batter can cause it to brown too quickly in a 450°F oven before it crisps up properly.
Drizzling 2 tbsp of oil over panko can be uneven; an oil spray would yield a more consistently crispy breading. Otherwise, the panko method is great for baked crispiness.
None. Deep-frying a flour/cornstarch batter is the most reliable way to achieve a truly crispy, 'better than takeout' texture.
